memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Everything in Israel that is devoted to the Lord is yours. The first offspring of every womb, both human and animal, that is offered to the Lord is yours. But you must redeem every firstborn son and every firstborn male of unclean animals. When they are a month old, you must redeem them at the redemption price set at five shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel, which weighs twenty gerahs." — Num 18:14-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The firstborn belonged to God in a special way. Every firstborn son had to be "redeemed" — bought back — with a payment of silver. This practice reached back to the exodus, when God had spared Israel's firstborn while judgment fell on Egypt. The firstborn belonged to God because He had rescued them, and now they were bought back into ordinary life.

This word "redeem" is one of the richest in all of Scripture. To redeem means to buy back, to secure release by paying a price. The firstborn were redeemed because they were seen as belonging to God, spared by His grace. A price had to be paid for their release, a tangible reminder that their lives were not their own.

Every one of these redemption payments was pointing forward, though the people may not have fully seen it. The whole practice whispered of a greater redemption to come — one that would not be paid in silver, but in something infinitely more costly.

Peter draws the line directly: we were redeemed "not with perishable things such as silver or gold... but with the precious blood of Christ." The redemption price for our lives was the blood of God's own Son. Like the firstborn of Israel, we belong to God because He has spared us and bought us back. But our redemption price was not five shekels; it was Calvary. You are not your own; you were bought at a price. Live today in the wonder of being redeemed, belonging fully to the God who paid so dearly for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What does it mean to you that your life has been "bought back" by God?
2. How does the costliness of your redemption shape how you live?
3. Does knowing you belong to God bring you comfort or challenge today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You have redeemed me, buying me back not with silver or gold but with the precious blood of Christ. I am not my own; I belong to You. Help me to live in the wonder of such costly love. Amen.
